r1_text: The buyer shall be able to view all MLS listings
r2_text: The buyer agent shall make only MLS listing that match the buyers criteria visible to the buyer.

phase2_cross_exam.challenge: The feasibility agent assumes that 'view all MLS listings' in Requirement A means authorization to the data pool rather than actual visibility, but this interpretation is not supported by the plain language of the requirement. The requirement states the buyer 'shall be able to view all MLS listings,' which directly conflicts with Requirement B's mandate that only matching listings be visible. The agent's coexistence path relies on redefining 'view' to mean 'have access to' rather than 'see,' which is an unsupported semantic shift that avoids rather than resolves the contradiction.

arbiter_reasoning: Requirement A says the buyer shall be able to view all MLS listings. Requirement B says only MLS listings matching the buyer's criteria shall be visible to the buyer. On the plain language, these impose conflicting visibility scopes for the same buyer: all listings versus only a subset. The feasibility-compatible reading depends on an unsupported reinterpretation of 'view all' as mere authorization rather than actual visibility.

r1_text: The system shall generate all the MLS numbers based on three criterias date, zone, and zip code.
r2_text: Relisting a previously sold house can reuse the same MLS number.

phase2_cross_exam.challenge: The feasibility agent's 'uncertain' verdict relies on an unstated assumption that the system could preserve the original listing date for a relisted property, which is not supported by the requirements and contradicts the typical interpretation of 'date' as the current listing date.

arbiter_reasoning: Requirement A says all MLS numbers shall be generated based on date, zone, and zip code. Requirement B allows a relisted previously sold house to reuse the same MLS number. For a relisting, the listing occurrence is new, so the date-based generation rule would produce a newly generated MLS number rather than reuse the old one. Because A applies to all MLS numbers and B permits an exception not stated in A, the requirements conflict.

r1_text: Buyer shall be able to generate a Comparative Market Analysis (CMA) report based on property criteria
r2_text: Only realators shall have access to CMA analysis and report generation

phase2_cross_exam.challenge: The Goal agent assumes 'Buyer' in Requirement A is a generic stakeholder interest rather than a system role with permissions, but this contradicts the plain language of the requirement which explicitly grants the Buyer the ability to generate the report. If Buyer is a distinct system role, then granting them this ability directly conflicts with Requirement B's restriction to realtors only.

arbiter_reasoning: Requirement A explicitly grants the Buyer the ability to generate a CMA report, while Requirement B restricts CMA analysis and report generation exclusively to realtors. On the plain language of the requirements, these refer to the same functionality and impose conflicting access rules. Without an explicit statement that every Buyer is also a realtor, both cannot be satisfied together.

r1_text: The system shall retrieve new raw data for Comparative Market Analysis (CMA) everytime a new house is sold in a given area
r2_text: The system shall retrieve the raw data for Comparative Market Analysis (CMA) once a week.

phase2_cross_exam.challenge: The logic agent claims the requirements are compatible by assuming Requirement B's 'once a week' is a minimum frequency, not an exclusive limit. However, the plain language 'once a week' typically implies exactly once per week, not 'at least once a week.' This reinterpretation is unsupported by the requirement text and directly enables the compatibility finding.

arbiter_reasoning: Requirement A requires retrieval on every house-sale event in the area, while Requirement B requires retrieval once a week for the same CMA raw data. The compatibility claim depends on reinterpreting 'once a week' as a non-exclusive minimum, but that is not supported by the text itself. Under the plain reading of the stated frequencies, the requirements prescribe conflicting retrieval schedules.

r1_text: Only the seller agent shall be able to marked an under contract MLS listing as sold.
r2_text: The agent shall be able to lookup and update any property listings in the MLS

phase2_cross_exam.challenge: The feasibility agent claims the requirements are compatible by assuming that 'update any' in Requirement B can be implemented to exclude the specific action restricted in Requirement A. However, this assumes an exception-based permission model that is not stated in either requirement. The plain language of Requirement B grants the ability to 'update any property listings' without qualification, which directly contradicts the exclusive restriction in Requirement A. The agent's coexistence path relies entirely on an unstated implementation detail rather than the actual text of the requirements.

arbiter_reasoning: Requirement A makes marking an under-contract MLS listing as sold exclusive to the seller agent. Requirement B says the agent can update any property listing in the MLS, and marking a listing as sold is a type of update. So B grants a broader permission that conflicts with A's exclusivity constraint.
